name: Civil unrest
summary: France's biggest day of protests in years on 5 Nov; strikes and protests continue, no deaths reported
state: More than 600,000 people marched across France on 5 Nov as unions struck over austerity and rising prices, the largest day of protests in years (Democracy Now; CNN). Protests continued on 6 Nov (Taipei Times). No deaths had been reported as of 6 Nov, so the Alert line of deadly nationwide unrest is not crossed.
for_you: Travellers to France may face transport strikes and demonstrations; FCDO travel advice for France lists current disruption.
rubric_hit: Watch: significant nationwide protests in France; no deadly unrest or crackdown

sources.title: CNN — Hundreds of thousands march in France's biggest day of protests in years
Democracy Now — Over 600,000 march in France as unions hold strike
Taipei Times — France hit by more protests, as workers go on strike

why: Mass protest and state crackdowns signal political fragility and can topple governments.
drivers: Cost of living, elections, corruption, repression, food and fuel prices.

rubric.alert: Deadly nationwide unrest or a state crackdown in a major country.
rubric.watch: Significant protests in several countries or deadly unrest in one.
rubric.normal: No deadly mass unrest in large countries.
